how: Explains requests for spare pixels and reinforcements without assuming that the recruited audience and the reported builders were the same group.
Explains a warning that the host venue is not very active without inferring that its canvas workers had measured their strength.
Explains the proposer's account of seeking permission because canvas space had run out.
Explains the objection to combining a wartime plane and a postwar flag as disagreement about the mark's representation.
Explains the report of expanding the lettering as visible evidence of building rather than an unanswered appeal alone.
Explains the anchor coordinates in the flag appeal without presuming that an agreed pixel template existed.
Explains defence appeals alongside construction and renewed recruitment rather than reducing the whole theme to maintenance.
Explains the correction and denial of the named attacker while leaving the actual source of changed pixels unsettled.
Explains a proposed spatial agreement that offers alternative positions and explicitly asks the host audience for permission.
Explains guest space seeking at the proposal stage without implying that the host granted permission or that the guest built.
Requires distinguishing presumed host permission from a realised hosted work when the request ends before an observed grant or build.
Makes realised guest building depend on placement still being open when recognition of closure ends the permission request.
Connects scarce space to asking another group for agreement through the proposer's explicit explanation rather than through a presumed relocation after loss.
Explains how recognising the canvas ending terminates an outstanding guest request before permission can lead to building.
Explains a proposer speaking for two named communities while leaving the mandate to represent them unverified.
Explains national history and nationalist concerns entering the choice of imagery without turning symbolic objection into an attack motive.
Requires evidence that a posting intervention targets canvas talk before treating generic approval and question redirection as canvas removal or a newly drawn boundary.

statement: Applying ordinary posting approval to canvas proposals
how: Explains the host's routine automatic approval filter without attributing a canvas-specific removal rule or opposition to the project.
Explains the minimal marking of the canvas ending without inferring preservation of a finished mark.
Explains recognising closure as the practical ending of a still-unfulfilled permission request and an occasion to apologise for bothering the host.
Explains a one-sided joke about an alleged attacker without implying an established rivalry or reciprocal taunting.
Keeps the target of disparagement provisional when the same exchange disputes who was attacking.
Leaves the project's starter and subsequent joining unobserved because an appeal for an existing defence does not identify who began it.
Leaves internal canvas order unresolved because calls and a progress report do not reveal how work was governed and posting moderation governs a different activity.
Leaves machine placement unobserved because the visible automatic tool moderates posts rather than placing pixels.
Leaves bare acceptance unobserved because the progress reply also requests reinforcements and cannot establish demand-free uptake.
Leaves restraint toward neighbours' art unobserved because the apology addresses bothering the audience after closure rather than canvas damage.
Leaves relocation after loss unobserved because the proposer describes seeking space without reporting an erased work or a move.
Leaves inter-room help transfer unobserved because the flag appeal identifies neither a completed transfer nor a distinct donor room.
Leaves coalition formation unobserved because naming two source communities does not establish an alliance with the host.
Leaves a pre-canvas tie naming an attack rival unobserved because national history appears in a design objection rather than an attack call.
Leaves an inherited quarrel unobserved because neither an institutional joke nor a symbolism objection establishes a prior inter-room dispute.
Leaves host April Fools parody unobserved because the flag appeal and generic moderation supply no evidence that the room treated these requests as a prank.
Leaves a completed-work celebration unobserved because the achievement report immediately requests further defence.
Leaves decisions about carrying the effort forward unobserved because ending one request does not establish what participants kept elsewhere.
Leaves initiated hostile action by the host unobserved because a defence call and a guest proposal seeking consent do not demonstrate such action.
Leaves disputes over who can bind the room unobserved because asking permission is answered with activity and symbolism concerns rather than a challenge to mandate.
Leaves disputes about a retained canvas version unobserved because the post-close exchange concerns a proposed symbol rather than cleanup or preservation.
Leaves call-caused building untested because the progress reply never attributes the expansion to the earlier call.
Leaves starter-caused recruitment untested because the appeal describes existing defence without identifying its origin.
Explains how reported expansion becomes work needing upkeep when returning blue prompts another reinforcement request within the same turn.
Leaves maintenance-caused negotiation untested because the later guest proposal does not recall or answer the earlier defence.
Leaves agreement-caused restraint untested because the guest request ends without a visible agreement or evidence of sparing art.
Leaves maintenance-to-machine escalation unobserved because the visible response to returning blue asks for reinforcements without mentioning placement automation.
Leaves building-to-completion celebration unobserved because the reported expansion remains under pressure rather than being announced finished.
Leaves celebration-to-recording untested because the ending is marked without a linked celebration or preservation request.
Leaves recording-to-continuation unobserved because marking closure ends the request without an expressed plan to carry it onward.
Leaves shortage-caused relocation untested because scarce space explains seeking consent rather than moving a lost work.
Leaves design-to-settling-template unobserved because the plane discussion concerns permission and symbolism without producing an agreed layout.
Leaves a call followed by bare acceptance unobserved because the visible progress response requests additional hands.
Leaves maintenance-to-inter-room-help transfer unobserved because the defence appeals do not report an identifiable other room sending help.
Leaves negotiation-to-help trading unobserved because the guest proposal ends without a deal or reported exchange of assistance.
Leaves recruitment-to-host-initiated attack unobserved because the calls request construction and defence rather than an offensive against a rival work.
Leaves attack-to-restraint untested because the permission request is not an observed attack and the later apology concerns bothering the host.
Leaves attack-caused negotiation untested because the visitor asks for consent without reporting a preceding attack.
Leaves attack-caused verbal contest untested because the institutional joke follows an attribution correction without establishing the alleged attack's source.
Leaves maintenance-to-coalition unobserved because repeated reinforcement requests do not establish joint defence agreements.
Requires canvas-directed moderation evidence before inferring that calls caused a flood and a new posting boundary from an ordinary automatic approval reply.
Leaves the tentative agreement-to-authority-dispute mechanism untested because no agreement or subsequent challenge to binding authority is observed.
